note: The ENGINEER's own scenario set for the safety lane (docs/design/intent-and-state.md, 4.5 and 8.2), written by the engineer BEFORE the phrase lists of apps/api/src/understand/lane.ts, family by family. It is a regression set, NOT the gate: the plan's gate wants positives written from scenarios by people who have not seen the lists (a clinician and a student). No method, means, dose, place or plan in any message (docs/eval/intent-writing-guide.md, 6.2). The independent check of the same families was written by a separate agent that never saw the lists (not in the repository).

cases.text: It has been a hard year. I lost my job in the spring, then my savings went, and since then every conversation at home has turned into an argument about money. My friends stopped calling a long time ago and I did not blame them, I was never good company. I wake up already tired and I go through the day like someone watching from outside. I used to read a lot. Now I open a book and the words slide off. My sister says I should see someone but I cannot imagine saying any of this out loud, so I am writing it here instead. Everything I try seems to make people more worried and I cannot stand being the reason for that. Honestly I think the people around me would manage better if I was not there, and I want to end my life.

cases.text: Background: Suicide is a leading cause of death among young adults. Methods: We conducted a systematic review of school-based prevention programmes published between 2000 and 2020, searching five databases. Two reviewers screened titles independently and extracted effect sizes. Results: Thirty-one studies met the inclusion criteria. Programmes that combined gatekeeper training with a referral pathway showed a modest reduction in self-reported ideation (pooled risk ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.94), whereas awareness campaigns alone showed no effect. Heterogeneity was high. Conclusions: Evidence for school-based programmes is limited and of low certainty.

cases.text: Objective: To describe the incidence and outcomes of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in an urban population. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Patients who collapsed in public places and received bystander resuscitation were compared with those who did not. We found that survival to discharge was 11.4% in the bystander group and 3.1% otherwise; patients who were unconscious on arrival and had a shockable rhythm had the best outcomes. Response times above eight minutes were associated with lower survival. We conclude that training lay responders is likely to improve outcomes, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.

cases.text: Self-harm is common in adolescents and is associated with later suicidal behaviour. In this narrative review we summarise cohort studies and trials of psychological interventions, including dialectical behaviour therapy and cognitive behavioural approaches. Most trials were small, follow-up was short, and few reported adverse events. Several observational studies suggest that restricting access to means reduces deaths at the population level, but these designs cannot establish causation. Future work should include larger trials, standardised outcome measures and the views of young people themselves.

cases.text: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially fatal systemic allergic reaction. Early recognition and intramuscular adrenaline are the cornerstone of management. In this audit of emergency department records we reviewed 214 presentations. Only 58% of patients with throat swelling or difficulty breathing received adrenaline within the first hour; delays were longer for children and for patients who presented with skin symptoms alone. We discuss barriers to timely treatment and propose a decision aid for triage nurses.
